bib.title: Can a Suit of Armor Conduct Electricity? A New Dataset for Open Book Question Answering
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2018 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 2381-2391

question: Can a QA dataset built around a small 'open book' of core science facts plus broad common knowledge expose the gap between systems and humans in multi-hop reasoning?
hypothesis: Existing retrieval/association-based science QA solvers will fail on questions that require combining an open-book fact with common knowledge, while humans solve them easily.
contributions: OpenBookQA: 5957 four-way multiple-choice elementary science questions with an open book of 1326 core facts
Multi-stage crowdsourcing pipeline with IR and word-association hardness filters and a crowd answerability filter
Baselines: pre-trained solvers, knowledge-free neural models showing dataset bias, and a knowledge-enhanced reader with oracle facts
A statistical estimate of human performance (~92%)

method.summary: Crowd workers on Mechanical Turk write a multiple-choice question from a core science fact f plus a self-chosen common fact k; questions failing IR and word-association solvers and answered by 4 of 5 other workers are kept. Baselines range from untrained science QA solvers to BiLSTM max-out models, a knowledge-enhanced reader and oracle-fact variants.
method.task: 4-way multiple-choice science question answering (open book + common knowledge)

datasets.name: OpenBookQA
datasets.size: 5957 questions; 1326 core facts F; ~6000 auxiliary facts K
datasets.split: 4957/500/500 Train/Dev/Test; Dev and Test additionally expert-filtered
datasets.source: Crowdsourced on Amazon Mechanical Turk (North America, masters qualification); F from WorldTree (Jansen et al. 2018); 8140 collected, 2183 discarded
datasets.preprocessing: Checks: exactly 4 choices, no negation words, uniform choice length (all <=3 or >=4 words); choices shuffled randomly

models.name: PMI, TableILP, TupleInference, DGEM, IR (pre-trained science solvers)
models.architecture: PMI over 280 GB text; ILP over tables; ILP over Open IE tuples; neural entailment

models.name: Embedd+Sim (L2 logistic regression)
models.architecture: Centroid GloVe vectors + cosine similarities, features in R^(5d+4)

models.name: BiLSTM max-out (Plausible Answer Detector, Odd-one-out, Question Match) and ESIM
models.architecture: BiLSTM max-out (Conneau et al. 2017) with linear attention Att(u,v)=W^T[u;v;u.v;|u-v|]

models.name: Knowledge-Enhanced Reader
models.architecture: Question Match BiLSTM max-out extended with attention over retrieved fact memory Mk; 9 attention terms with weights initialised to ones

other.knowledge_sources: F, WordNet, ConceptNet, oracle f, oracle k

training.objective: Multi-class classification over 4 labels (softmax over choice scores)
training.regularisation: L2 for the logistic regression baseline

other.note: Kingma and Ba 2015 (Adam), PyTorch and AllenNLP are cited in references but the body text does not state optimizer or hyperparameters; Appendix A not in PDF

inference.decoding: arg max over choice scores; ties score 1/k
inference.retrieval: IR over K to select a fixed-size subset K_Q,C per instance (details in Appendix A, not in PDF)

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: 1 point for correct answer, 1/k for a k-way tie including the correct answer; Guess All=25%

eval.protocol: Dev and Test; mean ± std over 5 seeds; human accuracy estimated from step-6 crowd answers with Hoeffding bound (H(Q)>=H~(Q)-3% with prob >98.8%, -2.5% with 95.6%)

evidence.quote: we report the former as our conservative estimate on human performance.

limits: Retrieving the right common knowledge is left open; the oracle k is author-written and noisy (incomplete, over-complete, or distantly related), not gold.
21% of analysed questions do not need the core fact.
Choice-only and odd-one-out baselines reach ~50%, showing annotation artifacts remain in the data.
Pre-trained solvers are correlated with the IR filter used to build the dataset, so their low scores are partly by design (IR gets 0% by construction).
Human estimate reuses the filtering annotations and assumes independent answers; worker dependence across questions left unanalysed.
Training hyperparameters (optimizer, lr, hidden size, epochs) not given in the body; appendices not in PDF.
Pre-LLM era models only (BiLSTM, GloVe, ELMo); modern LLMs not evaluated.

terms.definition: a set of 1326 elementary level science facts that forms the basis for generating the questions and is by itself generally insufficient to answer them
f: the core fact used by the question author; k: the author's additional fact for the question
